## Purpose

Use data from the CORA (COriolis Ocean Dataset for Reanalysis) project to compare OHC and heatwave trends to those produced from MOM6. We perform parallel analyses to those done in `explore_ohc.qmd`

## Import Data

```{r setup,include=F}
library(rnaturalearth)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)
library(terra)
library(here)
library(tidyterra)
library(viridis)
library(colorspace)
library(tictoc)
library(cowplot)

theme_set(theme_minimal()+theme(panel.border = element_rect(color='black',fill=NA)))
```

Ocean heat content has been calculated separately in `process_cora.R`. We calculated it across 5 depth bins: 0-50m, 50-100m, 100-250m, 250-500m, and 500-1000m depth

```{r}
ohc1 <- rast(here('output','cora_ohc_0_50_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc2 <- rast(here('output','cora_ohc_50_100_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc3 <- rast(here('output','cora_ohc_100_250_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc4 <- rast(here('output','cora_ohc_250_500_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc5 <- rast(here('output','cora_ohc_500_1000_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohcl <- list(ohc1,ohc2,ohc3,ohc4,ohc5)
```

Background polygon

```{r,warning=F}
coast <- ne_states(country='United States of America',returnclass = 'sf') |> 
  filter(name %in% c('California','Oregon','Washington','Nevada',"Idaho"))
coastcn <- ne_countries(country="Canada",scale=50,returnclass='sf')

coast <- st_union(coast,coastcn) |> 
  summarise() |> 
  st_transform(st_crs(ohc1)) |>
  st_crop(st_bbox(ohc1)) |> 
  st_shift_longitude()

# eez
eez <- read_sf(here('data','us_eez.shp')) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(ohc1)) |> 
  st_crop(st_bbox(ohc1)) |> 
  st_shift_longitude()
```

## Calculate Anomalies

Calculate a monthly climatology (mean and SD).

```{r}
ohc_climl <- map(ohcl,\(x) tapp(x,index='months',fun=mean))
ohc_clim_sdl <- map(ohcl,\(x) tapp(x,index='months',fun=sd))

names(ohc_climl) <- c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")
```

Calculate z-score anomalies by subtracting the mean and dividing by the SD

```{r}
anoml <- pmap(list(ohcl,ohc_climl,ohc_clim_sdl), \(x,y,z) (x - y)/z)
names(anoml) <- c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")
```

Example for the 0-50m depth layer, for June 2015. It's hot!

```{r}
ggplot()+
  geom_spatraster(data=anoml[[1]][[270]])+
  geom_sf(data=coast,fill="tan")+
  geom_sf(data=eez,fill=NA,color="black")+
  scale_fill_continuous_diverging(palette = "Blue-Red 2", mid = 0,
                                  na.value="gray90",limits=c(-3,3),oob=oob_squish) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0))+
  scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0))+
  labs(title=paste0("Ocean Heat Content 0-50m\n",time(ohc1)[270]),
       fill='Anomaly')
```

## Detrending

Let's make de-trended versions of the rasters, removing any linear effect of time on the anomalies. This will help us distinguish, e.g., short term deviations (heatwaves) from long-term warming.

```{r}
extract_trend <- function(rast_series, time_index=1:nlyr(rast_series)) {
  t_idx <- time_index
  
  trend <- app(rast_series, function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) return(rep(NA, length(x)))
    fit <- lm(x ~ t_idx)
    return(fitted(fit))
  })
  
  return(trend)
}

trendl <- map(anoml,extract_trend)
detrendl <- map2(anoml,trendl,\(x,y) x-y)
```

## Anomaly timeseries

Calculate an anomaly time series. First, a simple mean anomaly over time, averaging the anomaly values across all grid cells in a given time step and depth layer.

```{r}
timetbl <- tibble(date=time(ohc1)) |> 
  mutate(year=year(date),month=month(date))

# list of anomaly timeseries, for each depth bin
anom_ts <- imap(anoml,\(x,i) {
  global(x,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |>
    bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
    mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd,
           depth_layer=i)
  }) |> bind_rows()

ohc_ts <- imap(ohcl,\(x,i){
  global(x,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |>
    bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
    mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd,
           depth_layer=i)
}) |> bind_rows()


p_anom_ts <- anom_ts |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000"))) |>
  # filter(depth_layer==2) |>
  # filter(year<2025) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr,color=depthcat,
             fill=depthcat))+
  geom_ribbon(alpha=0.5,col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(5))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(5))+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="3 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="OHC Anomaly")+
  guides(fill='none',col='none')+
  facet_wrap(~depthcat,nrow=2)+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1,vjust=1))
p_anom_ts

p_ohc_ts <- ohc_ts |> 
  # filter(depth_layer==2) |>
  # filter(year<2025) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr,color=factor(depth_layer),
             fill=factor(depth_layer)))+
  geom_ribbon(alpha=0.5,col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(5))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(5))+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="3 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="OHC",fill="Depth\nLayer",col="Depth\nLayer")+
  facet_wrap(~factor(depth_layer),nrow=2,scales='free')+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1,vjust=1))
p_ohc_ts
```

## By Latitude

We can also make time series by latitude bins, to assess any latitudinal differences in the timing or magnitude of ocean heat changes.

```{r}
# make latitude bin raster
lat_rast <- anoml[[1]][[1]]  # Get one layer as template
values(lat_rast) <- NA
# Fill with latitude bin IDs
lat_breaks <- seq(32, 50, by=2)  # 2° bins
lat_labels <- paste(lat_breaks+1, "°N", sep = "")
zonetbl <- tibble(minlat=lat_breaks,maxlat=lead(lat_breaks)) |> 
                    mutate(zone=row_number())

# assign latitude bin ids to each raster cell
for (i in 1:nrow(lat_rast)) {
  cell_lat <- yFromCell(lat_rast, cellFromRowCol(lat_rast, i,1))
  bin_id <- cut(cell_lat, breaks=lat_breaks, labels=FALSE)
  lat_rast[i, ] <- bin_id
}
```

Use the latitude bin template raster and `terra::zonal()` to calculate latitude-bin means for all depth layers.

```{r}
# for each depth layer...
ts_by_lat <- imap(anoml,\(x,idx){
  # and for each time slice...
  imap(1:nlyr(x), \(t,n) {
    # ...calculate the mean anomaly value by latitude bin
    ldf <- zonal(x[[t]], lat_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
    tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],mean=ldf[,2])
    }) |> bind_rows() |> 
    mutate(depth_layer=idx)
}) |> bind_rows() |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")))

# detrended version
ts_by_lat_det <- imap(detrendl,\(x,idx){
  imap(1:nlyr(x), \(t,n) {
    ldf <- zonal(x[[t]], lat_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
    tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],mean=ldf[,2])
    }) |> bind_rows() |> 
    mutate(depth_layer=idx)
}) |> bind_rows() |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")))
```

Plot the time series by latitude bin.

```{r}
p_ts_by_lat <- ts_by_lat |> 
  mutate(date=timetbl$date[date]) |> 
  mutate(latlab=lat_labels[zone]) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=date,color=latlab))+
  geom_line(aes(y=mean))+
  facet_wrap(~depthcat,nrow=5)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(option="G")(9))+
  labs(x="Date",y="OHC Anomaly",color="Latitude\nBin")
p_ts_by_lat

# compare, e.g., around the southern california bight, around cape blanco, and around cape flaherty
p_ts_by_lat2 <- ts_by_lat |>
  filter(zone %in% c(1,6,9)) |>  
  mutate(latlab=lat_labels[zone]) |>
  mutate(date=timetbl$date[date]) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=date,color=latlab))+
  geom_line(aes(y=mean))+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("1997-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("1999-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("2014-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("2017-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  facet_wrap(~depthcat,nrow=5)+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(end=0.7,option="G")(3))+
  labs(x="Date",y="OHC Anomaly",color="Latitude\nBin",
       title="Mean OHC Anomaly by Depth and Latitude")
p_ts_by_lat2
```

## Heatwave Area

We can also calculate heatwave area. In our case, we'll define heatwave area as the total (summed) area of any grid cells in a given time step that have an anomaly value  greater than 1; that is, the total area greater than 1 SD above the long-term, monthly climatology.

```{r}
# terra calculates area correctly even with lat/lon coordinates,
# so we can just pull the area of each raster cell (which is in meters)
# and convert to sq. km
rarea <- cellSize(anoml[[1]])/1e6

calc_heatwave_area <- function(r,thresh=1){
  # find the area of all cells in heatwave
  rna <- ifel(r<thresh,NA,r)
  out <- mask(rarea,rna)
  global(out,sum,na.rm=T)
}
```

```{r}
heatwave_area_ts <- imap(anoml,\(x,y){
  area <- sapply(x,calc_heatwave_area,thresh=1)
  tibble(date=timetbl$date,area=unlist(area),
         depth_layer=y)
}) |> bind_rows()

# de-trended version
heatwave_area_detrend_ts <- imap(detrendl,\(x,y){
  area <- sapply(x,calc_heatwave_area,thresh=1)
  tibble(date=timetbl$date,area=unlist(area),
         depth_layer=y)
}) |> bind_rows()

p_hw_area <- heatwave_area_ts |>
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000"))) |> 
  mutate(doy=yday(date),year=year(date)) |> 
  # filter(year %in% c(1997,2014,2019,2020,2022,2023,2024,2025)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,area/1e5,color=depthcat))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(option="G",begin=0.2,end=0.8)(5))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("1997-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("1999-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("2014-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("2017-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  facet_wrap(~depthcat,nrow=5,scales='free_y')+
  guides(color='none')+
  scale_x_date(expand=c(0,0),date_breaks = "3 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y=expression("Area in Heatwave Conditions (10"^"5" ~ "km"^"2"~")"),
       color="Depth")

p_hw_area_det <- heatwave_area_detrend_ts |>
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000"))) |> 
  mutate(doy=yday(date),year=year(date)) |> 
  # filter(year %in% c(1997,2014,2019,2020,2022,2023,2024,2025)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,area/1e5,color=depthcat))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(option="G",begin=0.2,end=0.8)(5))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("1997-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("1999-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("2014-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  geom_vline(xintercept=as_date("2017-01-01"),linetype=2)+
  facet_wrap(~depthcat,nrow=5,scales='free_y')+
  guides(color='none')+
  scale_x_date(expand=c(0,0),date_breaks = "3 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y=expression("Area in Heatwave Conditions (10"^"5" ~ "km"^"2"~")"),
```
